advances: A refinement of a given actual marked coupling with fixed full original marginals.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let $B$ have columns $(1,q)$. In $A_p=\{a\ge0:Ba=(1,p)\}$, a dependent positive support admits a nonzero kernel vector supported there and hence opposite small feasible perturbations. Conversely, if $a$ is a midpoint of feasible vectors, both vanish off its support, so independent columns force equality. Solving for a vertex on a nonsingular square minor of the integer matrix gives rational entries. There are finitely many supports and $\operatorname{rank}B=1+\dim\operatorname{aff}P$. Take the least common multiple of denominators. Every $a$ decomposes into vertices: on a dependent support the kernel vector has both signs since its coordinate sum is zero. Moving in both directions until the first zero expresses $a$ using vectors of smaller support, so induction terminates. The self-template $e_p$ is a vertex. Any other vertex has zero $p$-weight, since a $p$-weight strictly between zero and one splits off that share of $e_p$ and leaves another anchored probability vector.

To choose coefficients $\theta_r(a)$ Borelly, list the affinely independent nonempty vertex sublists and select the first whose closed hull contains $a$. They cover $A_p$ because any dependent convex representation can lose a coefficient by movement along an affine dependence. The barycentric coordinates on the selected simplex are continuous there and the finitely many choice regions are Borel.

Disintegrate $\gamma$ at its input $a=(u,p,x)$ on the compact standard Borel spaces in the statement. Write $w_q(a)$ for the conditional probability at target base $q$ and $y_q(a)$ for its continuous mean conditional on that base when $w_q>0$. Null branches may use a fixed point of $K_q$. These functions have Borel versions. The marked target support and preservation of $u$ give $y_q(a)\in F_q(u)$ on positive branches. On a common full source set, $w$ is in $A_p$ and $\sum_q w_qy_q=x$. Decompose $w=\sum_r\theta_r\alpha^{p,r}$. For $\theta_r>0$ put $z_r=\sum_q\alpha^{p,r}_q y_q$; every positive term has $w_q>0$. Compatibility gives $z_r\in K_p$ and $\sum_q\alpha^{p,r}_q h_q(u)\le h_p(u)$. Their $\theta$-average equals $u\cdot\sum_q w_q y_q=h_p(u)$, so each used template has equality. Compatibility and that equality prove actual face inclusion for every choice of the component face points. Also $\sum_r\theta_r z_r=x$.

On original pairs with source base $p$ and target base $q$ attach template $r$ with Borel weight $\theta_r\alpha^{p,r}_q/w_q$, set to zero when $w_q=0$. These weights lie in $[0,1]$ and sum to one almost everywhere under $\gamma$, since the first marginal of its target-base-$q$ restriction is $w_q\nu$. Attach $(u,p,z_r,r)$ to the resulting law. The $r,q$ branch has original input marginal $\theta_r\alpha^{p,r}_q\nu$ on base $p$ and continuous first moment $\theta_r\alpha^{p,r}_q y_q\nu$. Hence the first stage retains the base and normal and has conditional continuous mean $x$. For each original input and positive template the target law has base probabilities $\alpha^{p,r}$ and mean $(p,z_r)$. Testing against Borel functions of the intermediate proves the same statements on the projected second stage, even when several inputs give the same intermediate mark. Summing the weights recovers the entire original pair law. Markov composition of the projected stages need not recover the original pair dependence. Multiply the anchored equations and face inclusion by $D$ to obtain the integer statement. Extremality and $\sum_r\theta_r z_r=x$ force $z_r=x$ on all positive branches. For zero mass take the zero triple measure.
statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, and let the nonempty compact convex sets $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, satisfy $\sum_q a_qK_q\subset K_p$ for every probability vector $a$ on $P$ of barycenter $p\in P$. Write $h_p(u)=h_{K_p}(u)$ and $F_p(u)=\{x\in K_p:u\cdot x=h_p(u)\}$ for a unit normal $u$. Let $\gamma$ be a finite same-normal martingale on the compact marked bundle of $(u,p,x)$ with $x\in F_p(u)$, in the physical coordinates $(p,x)$, with source $\nu$ and target $\eta$.

For each $p$ there are finitely many templates $\alpha^{p,r}$, the vertices of the probability polytope with barycenter $p$. They have rational entries, a common integer denominator $D$ depending only on $P$, and support of size at most $1+\dim\operatorname{aff}P$. There is a measure on triples of original input, marked intermediate $(u,p,z,r)$ with $z\in F_p(u)$, and original output, whose input-output projection is exactly $\gamma$. The first stage is a same-normal martingale preserving the base and the second is a same-normal physical martingale. On every intermediate base and template $(p,r)$, the first marginal of the second-stage restriction to target base $q$ is $\alpha^{p,r}_q$ times the intermediate law on $(p,r)$. At almost every used intermediate mark, $\sum_q\alpha^{p,r}_q h_q(u)=h_p(u)$ and $\sum_q\alpha^{p,r}_q F_q(u)\subset F_p(u)$. Thus the integer multiplicities $D\alpha^{p,r}_q$ have sum $D$, base sum $Dp$ and corresponding Minkowski face sum in $D F_p(u)$. If $\nu$-almost every source $x$ is extreme in $K_p$, then its intermediate point equals $x$ almost surely.
title: Finite rational marked templates of a given boundary martingale
